course_name_original: Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales II (21720028)
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials II
prerequisites: Having taken the course Elasticity and Strength of Materials I
Having passed the course Elasticity and Strength of Materials I

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Competence in applying ethical principles related to sustainability values in personal and professional behaviors.
Competence in the sustainable use of resources and in preventing negative impacts on the natural and social environment.
Interpret the resistant problem: reality, equations, and safety coefficients.
Know the fundamentals and limitations of sizing resistant elements.
Introduce the student to the new regulations.
Know and use the principles of elasticity.

syllabus_topics: Block I - Elasticity: Topic 1. Stresses. Introduction to elasticity. Exterior forces and interior forces. Stress vector at a point. Intrinsic and global components. Study of stress vectors at a point. Stress matrix. Change of reference system. Principal stresses and directions. Properties. Mohr's circles. Equilibrium equations. Maximum and minimum values of normal stress and tangential stress. Octahedral stresses. Lamé's stress ellipsoid.

Block I - Elasticity: Topic 2. Deformations. Introduction. State of deformation of a mechanical prism. Decomposition of the deformation matrix. Spherical matrix and deviatoric matrix. Compatibility equations.

Block I - Elasticity: Topic 3. Relations between stresses and deformations. Relation between stress and deformation states. Stress-strain diagram. Hooke's Law. Transversal deformations. Poisson's coefficient. Principle of superposition. Generalized Hooke's Law. Lamé's equations.

Block II - Resistencia de Materiales: Topic 1: Skew bending and combined bending. - Skew bending in the elastic domain. Stress analysis. Deformation analysis. - Combined bending. - Eccentric tension or compression. - Combined bending in slender beams. - Central core of the section.
Block II - Resistencia de Materiales: Topic 2: Hyperstatic bending. - Calculation of single-span beams. - Calculation of continuous beams.
Block II - Resistencia de Materiales: Topic 3: Torsional stress. - Torsion in elements of non-circular section.
Block II - Resistencia de Materiales: Topic 4: Methods for calculating the deformed shape. - Mohr's theorems. - Conjugate beam theorem. - Supports with settlements (spring).

Block II - Resistencia de Materiales: Topic 5: Extension of concepts. - Triangular and trapezoidal loads. - Beams with variable section. - Composite structures (cellular beams, double U composite columns, etc).
Block II - Resistencia de Materiales: Topic 6: Structural reinforcements. - Cover plates and stiffeners.
teaching_methods: Computer practices: Resolution of exercises and problems. Application of a Finite Element Method program for the analysis and resolution of Strength of Materials exercises and the interpretation of results.
Non-contact training activities: Hours of study and personal work.
Tutorials: Face-to-face or virtual campus personal or collective tutorials.
Other activities: Oral presentations of specific cases. Computer-based works. Final exam of the course.

Practical classes, seminars and problems: Resolution of exercises. Problem-based learning. Application of knowledge in specific exercises, with didactic content to deepen and broaden theoretical knowledge, with special emphasis on self-learning. Students develop appropriate solutions, follow procedures and interpret results.

Theoretical-practical classes: Expository method/master class, face-to-face or using Flipped Classroom. Case study. Resolution of exercises. The professor explains the competencies and objectives to be achieved: Basic contents of a topic are taught in a structured way. Typical exercises and particular cases are presented to consolidate contents. Problem-based learning: Application activities are developed.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance to computer practices and autonomous work
Final face-to-face test to evaluate the overall learning outcome of the course by the student
Progress tests will be carried out according to the subject matter
Completion of assignments proposed by the professor

assessment_rules: Attendance to computer practices is mandatory to take the final face-to-face exam. The final face-to-face test accounts for 60% of the grade, progress tests for 20%, autonomous work from computer practices for 10%, and proposed assignments for 10%. The student's personal work is a fundamental and essential part of their learning process.
